reference: No pax executable is available in the reference PATH. Where no pax CLI exists, parity scripts use GNU tar 1.35 for the shared USTAR list/create/extract behavior and GNU cp -a for the bounded pax -rw file-tree analogue; cases state this mapping explicitly and do not claim full GNU pax compatibility. Fixed extraction inputs are valid USTAR archives emitted by Python standard-library tarfile, independently of the candidate. The harness requires the named GNU commands before running each parity case.
coverage: List and extract fixed USTAR regular-file archives encoded by Python tarfile.
Extraction from a pipe across multiple padded member bodies.
Directory, regular file, hard link, and relative symlink extraction.
Create and list archives containing empty and nonempty regular files.
Recursive directory archive round-trip-result comparison, plus independent tarfile member decoding.
Bounded -rw copy mode over a relative directory tree.
exclusions: No GNU pax executable is installed; GNU tar and GNU cp references cover only their explicitly stated common file/archive semantics.
No absolute paths, device members, absolute or parent-traversing archive members, privileged operations, network access, or system state are exercised.
Raw USTAR timestamp/header padding bytes are not asserted equal; complete semantic member data, types, modes and link targets are independently decoded for creation cases.

Distinct source inodes mapped onto one archive pathname can make a later hardlink alias bind to the replacement data, as independently observed with GNU tar. General preservation of source data/topology across conflicting archive member names is not claimed.

cases.purpose: Check the documented Bash loadable contract: pax resolves as a builtin and help returns nonempty command documentation. This is metadata coverage, not operation coverage.

List two regular members from a fixed USTAR archive emitted by Python tarfile, an independent encoder. Candidate pax listing is compared with GNU tar listing for the common USTAR member-name behavior; the archive contains no directory entries whose trailing-slash display differs between tools.
Extract regular members from the independent USTAR archive, including an implicit parent directory, and compare resulting paths, bytes, and modes with GNU tar extraction.
Read the independent multi-member archive through a pipe. The non-block-sized first body tests that extraction consumes its padding and continues to the next member, a documented pax regression area.

Extract USTAR directory, regular-file, hard-link, and relative symlink entries from an independent Python tarfile archive. Compare file data, modes, hard-link identity, and symlink target with GNU tar.

Create an archive containing an empty and a nonempty regular file, then compare member listings. GNU tar creates the reference USTAR archive and lists it; pax creates and lists its own archive. Archive byte identity is not claimed because USTAR metadata layout is not a semantic guarantee; member listing and independent decoding inspect the retained archive. The raw archive is retained. compare_tree is false because valid USTAR headers contain varying timestamps and implementation-specific padding; an independent tarfile decoder below emits every member type, mode, link target and regular-file payload, with no metadata normalization of those compared fields.
cases.script:
printf 'payload\n' > first
: > empty
if [[ $(type -t pax) == builtin ]]; then
  pax -w -f result.tar first empty
  pax -f result.tar
else
  tar --format=ustar -cf result.tar first empty
  tar -tf result.tar
fi

/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PYVERIFY'
import tarfile
with tarfile.open('result.tar', 'r:') as archive:
 for member in archive:
  print(repr((member.name, member.type, member.mode, member.linkname, archive.extractfile(member).read() if member.isfile() else None)))
PYVERIFY

/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PYTREE'
from pathlib import Path
import stat
links={}
for path in sorted(Path('.').rglob('*')):
 if str(path)=='result.tar': continue
 info=path.lstat()
 kind=stat.S_IFMT(info.st_mode)
 data=path.read_bytes() if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) else (str(path.readlink()) if path.is_symlink() else None)
 link=links.setdefault((info.st_dev,info.st_ino),str(path)) if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) else None
 print(repr((str(path),kind,stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode),data,link)))
PYTREE

cases.purpose: Archive a small directory recursively with a regular file and relative symlink, then extract under a separate directory. The reference uses GNU tar create/extract for the same USTAR tree behavior; output checks and the independent filesystem manifest require the nested file and symlink to survive. The raw archive is retained. compare_tree is false because valid USTAR headers contain varying timestamps and implementation-specific padding; an independent tarfile decoder below emits every member type, mode, link target and regular-file payload, with no metadata normalization of those compared fields.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/sub extracted
printf 'nested payload\n' > source/sub/file
ln -s file source/sub/link
if [[ $(type -t pax) == builtin ]]; then
  pax -w -f result.tar source
  (cd extracted && pax -r -f ../result.tar)
else
  tar --format=ustar -cf result.tar source
  (cd extracted && tar --no-same-owner -xf ../result.tar)
fi
[[ $(<extracted/source/sub/file) == 'nested payload' ]]
[[ -L extracted/source/sub/link ]]
[[ $(<extracted/source/sub/link) == 'nested payload' ]]
printf 'nested=%s\nsymlink=yes\n' "$(<extracted/source/sub/file)"

/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PYVERIFY'
import tarfile
with tarfile.open('result.tar', 'r:') as archive:
 for member in archive:
  print(repr((member.name, member.type, member.mode, member.linkname, archive.extractfile(member).read() if member.isfile() else None)))
PYVERIFY

/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PYTREE'
from pathlib import Path
import stat
links={}
for path in sorted(Path('.').rglob('*')):
 if str(path)=='result.tar': continue
 info=path.lstat()
 kind=stat.S_IFMT(info.st_mode)
 data=path.read_bytes() if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) else (str(path.readlink()) if path.is_symlink() else None)
 link=links.setdefault((info.st_dev,info.st_ino),str(path)) if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) else None
 print(repr((str(path),kind,stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode),data,link)))
PYTREE

cases.purpose: Exercise pax -rw copy mode on a bounded relative directory tree with a file and symlink. In this environment without a pax executable, GNU cp -a is an independent file-copy oracle for the same paths, contents, modes, and symlink target; this does not claim complete POSIX pax copy semantics.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/sub dest
printf 'copy payload\n' > source/sub/file
ln -s file source/sub/link
if [[ $(type -t pax) == builtin ]]; then
  pax -rw source dest
else
  cp -a source dest
fi
[[ $(<dest/source/sub/file) == 'copy payload' ]]
[[ -L dest/source/sub/link ]]
[[ $(<dest/source/sub/link) == 'copy payload' ]]
printf 'copied=%s\nsymlink=yes\n' "$(<dest/source/sub/file)"

cases.purpose: A short, malformed archive must be rejected with a diagnostic. This checks the documented archive-validation contract without asserting GNU tar exit-code or diagnostic wording, since no GNU pax CLI is installed.
cases.script:
printf 'short archive' > broken.tar
if pax -f broken.tar; then
  printf 'accepted\n'
  exit 1
else
  printf 'rejected\n'
fi

cases.purpose: Pax creation emits regular hardlinks and FIFO metadata readable by GNU tar; a later archive containing only an alias has its own fresh context.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/mkdir restored one-member
printf shared > original
/usr/bin/ln original twin
/usr/bin/mkfifo -m 0640 pipe
pax -w -f archive.tar original twin pipe
/usr/bin/tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
[[ restored/original -ef restored/twin && -p restored/pipe && $(<restored/original) == shared ]]
pax -w -f next.tar twin
/usr/bin/tar -xf next.tar -C one-member
[[ $(<one-member/twin) == shared ]]
printf 'pax writer links fifo and context verified\n'
cases.stdout: pax writer links fifo and context verified

cases.purpose: The shared pax reader extracts fixed independent FIFO metadata without opening a stream and preserves its normal pax mode contract despite umask077.
cases.script:
printf '%s' '' | /usr/bin/base64 -d > oracle.tar
/usr/bin/mkdir restored
umask 077
(cd restored; pax -r -f ../oracle.tar)
[[ -p restored/pipe && $(<restored/after) == 'fifo sibling' ]]
/usr/bin/stat -c %a restored/pipe restored/after
: > after-mask
/usr/bin/stat -c %a after-mask
